text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes treatment involves lifestyle changes, regular blood sugar monitoring, and medications to help keep your glucose in a safe range.
snippet_highlighted_words: lifestyle changes, regular blood sugar monitoring, and medications

list.snippet: Healthy diet: Eat more vegetables, lean proteins, and complex carbohydrates with fiber while limiting sugary foods.
Physical activity: Try to get at least 150 minutes of exercise each week, like brisk walking.
Weight management: Losing a small amount of extra body weight can greatly improve how your body handles blood sugar.

Metformin: This is usually the first oral pill prescribed by doctors. It lowers the sugar your liver makes and helps your body use insulin better. You can read more about it through the Mayo Clinic treatment guide.
GLP-1 receptor agonists: These are injectable drugs that help your body release insulin and slow digestion to lower blood sugar and help with weight loss.
SGLT2 inhibitors: These pills help your kidneys remove extra sugar through your urine.

Other oral drugs: Options like sulfonylureas or DPP-4 inhibitors help your pancreas make more insulin or keep digestion chemicals active. Explore further drug classes on the American Diabetes Association portal.
Insulin therapy: If other treatments are not enough, you may need daily insulin injections to control your glucose.
Checking levels: Use a standard blood glucose meter or a continuous glucose monitor (CGM) to track how food and activity affect your body in real time.
